_comment: Committed baseline for benchmarks/check_regression.py (T3, calibrated per F-067). Generated by running the 'ci_guard' cell six times back-to-back as separate subprocesses on the development machine below. Each run times the engine and a fixed reference kernel interleaved in the same process; the guard compares engine/reference now against then, so a machine that is uniformly slower cancels out. The ratio's run-to-run spread is tighter than either timing's alone, which is the calibration working: a run slowed by machine state slows both. Verified on real slower hardware by pinning the run to this chip's efficiency cores: raw engine time rose 4.56x (40.08 ms to 182.68 ms), which would fail an uncalibrated 3.0x guard with no code changed, while the ratio moved 0.06% (2.6998 to 2.6981). Efficiency and performance cores share an architecture and a BLAS, so a move to x86 CI hardware can shift the ratio more than that; the 3.0x factor leaves room for it. Between sessions the ratio median itself drifted about 6% (2.54 here, 2.70 a minute later), also well inside the factor.
